That’s a very common assumption, and Connecticut’s system makes it confusing.

There is a primary date scheduled every cycle, but for U.S. House seats in Connecticut, a primary only actually happens if a challenger first gets on the ballot. In practice, that has almost never occurred.

In fact, Connecticut has never had a contested Democratic primary for a U.S. House seat against an incumbent, including in CT-03. The one notable exception at the federal level was the U.S. Senate race in 2006.

Under state law, the only way to trigger a real primary for this seat is through a petition signed by registered Democrats. That’s why this effort exists — not to support or oppose anyone, but to make the choice possible in the first place.
